```luau
--!strict
-- JuiceService: server side of the juice/polish pass.
-- Sets up lighting, the JuiceFx / JuiceAck remotes, and fires juice events to clients.

local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")

local GameAssets = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("GameAssets"))
local ForgeTelemetry = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("ForgeTelemetry"))

local JuiceService = {}

local ACK_COOLDOWN = 5

local inited = false
local fxRemote: RemoteEvent? = nil
local ackRemote: RemoteEvent? = nil
local lastAck: { [Player]: number } = {}

local function ensureRemote(name: string): RemoteEvent
	local existing = ReplicatedStorage:FindFirstChild(name)
	if existing and existing:IsA("RemoteEvent") then
		return existing
	end
	local r = Instance.new("RemoteEvent")
	r.Name = name
	r.Parent = ReplicatedStorage
	return r
end

local function fire(player: Player, payload: { [string]: any })
	if not fxRemote or not player or player.Parent ~= Players then
		return
	end
	fxRemote:FireClient(player, payload)
	ForgeTelemetry.count("juice_events", 1)
end

local function toPart(inst: any): BasePart?
	if typeof(inst) ~= "Instance" then
		return nil
	end
	if inst:IsA("BasePart") then
		return inst
	end
	if inst:IsA("Model") then
		if inst.PrimaryPart then
			return inst.PrimaryPart
		end
		return inst:FindFirstChildWhichIsA("BasePart", true)
	end
	return nil
end

function JuiceService.init()
	if inited then
		return
	end
	inited = true

	local ok, err = pcall(function()
		GameAssets.styleLighting()
	end)
	if not ok then
		warn("[JuiceService] styleLighting failed: " .. tostring(err))
	end

	fxRemote = ensureRemote("JuiceFx")
	local ack = ensureRemote("JuiceAck")
	ackRemote = ack

	ack.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player: Player, payload: any)
		if typeof(player) ~= "Instance" or not player:IsA("Player") then
			return
		end
		if type(payload) ~= "table" or payload.kind ~= "income" then
			return
		end
		local now = os.clock()
		local last = lastAck[player]
		if last and now - last < ACK_COOLDOWN then
			return
		end
		lastAck[player] = now
		ForgeTelemetry.count("income_shown", 1)
	end)

	Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(player: Player)
		lastAck[player] = nil
	end)
end

-- upgrade: entry from Upgrades data. padPart: the pad touched. newDropperModel: the dropper
-- that was just unlocked (Model or BasePart) or nil.
function JuiceService.onPurchase(player: Player, upgrade: any, padPart: any, newDropperModel: any)
	if type(upgrade) ~= "table" then
		return
	end
	local dropperPart = toPart(newDropperModel)
	if dropperPart then
		local ok, err = pcall(function()
			GameAssets.popIn(dropperPart)
		end)
		if not ok then
			warn("[JuiceService] popIn failed: " .. tostring(err))
		end
	end

	local name = tostring(upgrade.name or upgrade.id or "Upgrade")
	local pos: Vector3? = nil
	if typeof(padPart) == "Instance" and padPart:IsA("BasePart") then
		pos = padPart.Position
	end
	fire(player, { kind = "buy", name = name, pos = pos })

	local isOre = upgrade.ore or upgrade.oreTier or upgrade.isOre
	if isOre then
		local value = upgrade.oreValue or upgrade.value or 0
		fire(player, { kind = "ore", name = name, value = value })
	end
end

function JuiceService.onInsufficient(player: Player, upgrade: any, shortfall: number)
	if type(shortfall) ~= "number" or shortfall ~= shortfall then
		return
	end
	fire(player, { kind = "poor", need = math.max(0, math.ceil(shortfall)) })
end

function JuiceService.onRebirth(player: Player)
	fire(player, { kind = "rebirth" })
end

function JuiceService.pushGoal(player: Player, name: string?, cost: number?)
	if name == nil or cost == nil then
		fire(player, { kind = "goal" })
		return
	end
	fire(player, { kind = "goal", name = name, cost = cost })
end

return JuiceService

```

## Lessons from past builds
# Lessons
## Design
- Tune early progression so a playtest of roughly 15 seconds can reach the first purchase or milestone. Use a fast starting income or a cheap first upgrade (a few seconds of income). Slow openings leave the buy loop untested and feel dull. Keep the second purchase within about 20-30s of idle income, by raising per-item value or lowering the price. Chain the first few upgrades so there is always something affordable to chase in the first minute, with no long dead gaps.
- Starting cash must be strictly below the first upgrade's price, never equal to it. An instant spend gives the player no chase and no sense of what cubes are for. Start slightly below the price so the first few collected cubes earn it, within about 10s. Check starter cash against the first cost in config before finishing.
- The first purchase must actually happen in a short playtest, and its counters (e.g. upgrades_bought) must be above 0. If the report lacks them, the first pad is too hard to find or reach. A highlight or "affordable" counter above 0 with no purchase counter means the pad was reachable in logic but the player never touched it. Put the first pad close to where the player stands after claiming (just off the walking path), and guide the player to it with a beam. Make sure the tutorial step that points to it fires.
- Assume the playtest player may stand idle. Enough cash alone is not enough: the first pad must be within a few studs of the post-claim position, or a fallback must buy or prompt the first upgrade after the player has been able to afford it for a few seconds. Otherwise the purchase loop goes untested even though cubes were collected.
- Give per-event feedback for every economy action: a "+N" popup on collect, plus HUD hints for upgrade cost, affordability or progress. Without it, numbers going up feels weak between purchases. Add a visible next-goal indicator, such as a progress bar toward the next affordable upgrade, and pulse the cash counter on each gain.
- Give failure feedback as well as success feedback. A pad, button, shop purchase or rebirth attempted without enough cash, or a shop card whose requirement is not owned, needs a red flash, an audible buzz, a shake and a "Need $N" or requirement toast, debounced to about 1s. Never return silently from a denied Buy handler. A silent denial confuses young players.
- Place trigger pads (buy pads, claim gates, etc.) off the spawn path so walking from spawn never fires them accidentally. They must still be easy to find and reach: guide the player to the first pad with a visible beam or arrow.
- Make moving cubes or other spawned items non-colliding with players (CanCollide = false, or a collision group) and cap their count per area. Otherwise they jitter, stick or knock players around.
- Keep the time to first core-loop activity well inside the playtest window (the probe may last only ~6-15s). Any auto-claim or auto-start fallback must fire within about 3-5s, never 20s. A spec or acceptance text that says 20s is wrong for playtests, so shorten it and keep the tested window consistent. Claim gates should sit near the spawn area, not far outside the plaza. An idle player must still reach the loop quickly. Auto-claim can mask an unreachable gate, so place gates where an idle spawn can plausibly touch them.
- Budget the whole first-payout path, not just the claim: claim delay + first spawn + conveyor travel (length / speed) should land the first cash-in within about 3-4s of the claim. Use a short, fast conveyor, spawn the first item immediately on claim, and don't leave this borderline.
- Keep tutorial text consistent with the actual flow (e.g. don't say "walk to a gate" if auto-claim happens within seconds). Tutorial steps must be advanced by events that actually occur, or the player is left without guidance. Add a time-based fallback so a step can't stall.
